questions.text: How does a globe help in learning Geography?
questions.text_as_printed: How does a globe help in learning Geography? (Difficult)

answer.value:
The globe helps me in the learning of geography subject in the following ways:
a) Helps to know the shape of the Earth.
b) Aids in understanding the position, size, and shape of continents, oceans, and seas on the Earth's surface.
c) Helps to know the exact location and political boundaries using latitudes and longitudes.
d) Helps to understand Earth's axis tilt, Earth's movements, daily and annual movements, and their effects.
e) From the globe, we can know various geographical features on the Earth's surface (mountains, plateaus, plains, deserts, etc.).

questions.text: List the uses of maps.
questions.text_as_printed: List the uses of maps. (Difficult)

answer.value:
Uses of Maps:
a) Maps help us to know the location of cities, districts, states, countries, continents, etc.
b) Useful for showing physical features like mountains, plateaus, deserts, coastal areas, islands, etc.
c) Helpful to understand transportation connections of regions.
d) Help to know the distribution of crops, minerals, industries, etc.
e) Very useful to soldiers during war and defense situations.
f) Provide guidance to tourists.
g) These are important teaching and learning tools, and they can be easily carried from one place to another.

questions.text: Ravi was returning home after school in the evening. He first walked in the direction from which the Sun rises, then turned to his right, and again turned to his left before reaching his home. Observe and write the directions in which he travelled to reach his home.
questions.text_as_printed: Ravi was returning home after school in the evening. He first walked in the direction from which the Sun rises, then turned to his right, and again turned to his left before reaching his home. Observe and write the directions in which he travelled to reach his home. (Difficult)

answer.value:
Initial stage (Starting direction): He started from the direction where the sun rises, i.e. he started from the East and was facing towards the West (the opposite direction).
First turn (Right): While walking facing West, if he turns right he will face North; now he is moving towards the North.
Second turn (Left): While walking facing North, if he again turns left he will face West once more.
Conclusion: Starting from the East (walking towards the West), turning North, and finally moving West, he reaches his house.
